items.author: Claude (Ben, 2026-11-14: "try implementing the easier changes first")
items.title: Spike: can the ground hold GPU-compressed chunks, for a finer master in the same RAM
items.design: RENDERING.md § Resident set. Every AAA reference stores terrain BC1/BC7-compressed: four to eight times less memory per pixel, so a 192 px master would fit today's budget. UNKNOWN: whether an SDL_Renderer texture can be uploaded compressed (likely not; the GPU API can). WORK: a spike that answers that and measures encode cost per chunk; lossy, so the 6 GB ceiling and capture determinism are both on the table. SPIKE 2026-11-14: SDL 3.4's GPU renderer wraps an external SDL_GPUTexture (SDL_PROP_TEXTURE_CREATE_GPU_TEXTURE_POINTER), so a BC1/BC7 chunk can draw on the GPU path, never in software captures. Measuring encode cost needs a vendored encoder; NR-1233 holds the call. Ben, 2026-11-16 (NR-1233 option A): vendor stb_dxt (BC1, public domain) and MEASURE encode ms per 512 px chunk only; the format decision follows the numbers. READING 2026-11-16 (tools/verify/bc1_encode_measure.cpp, stb_dxt v1.13 vendored at third_party/stb/stb_dxt.h, 18 chunks of 512 px from the ground previews): BC1 encodes in a median 3.32 ms a chunk on one core (high-quality mode 3.60 ms), PSNR 41.1 dB median (38.8 worst), worst channel error 54 at a structure edge; by eye the loss is the finest grain noise. A 2.9 GB chain re-encodes in about 13 s of one core, about 1 s across the bake pool, and holds about 0.5 GB. CLOSED UNBUILT (Ben, 2026-11-17, NR-1237 option B): nothing binds on ground memory today; reopen from these numbers when it does.

items.author: Claude (Ben, 2026-11-19: generation speed ideas; "file 1 and 4")
items.title: Score the landscape search's proposals ahead, in parallel, so "Placing buildings" waits on one evaluation instead of four
items.design: MEASURED 2026-11-19 (seed 0, Release): "Placing buildings" is ~10.8 s, of which ~8.1 s is four landscape evaluations run one after another (the seed candidate and three placement rounds, ~2.0 s each); the rest is the winner's apply, the majors reconcile and the retrofit. The walk is serial in its DECISIONS, not its candidates: a round's proposal is perturb_placement(incumbent, axis_rng(seed, round)), keyed not sequenced, so after k rounds the incumbent is one of at most 2^k candidates and the whole proposal tree for the next D rounds is known before any is scored. WORK: score that tree at once (2^D - 1 proposals, plus the seed in the first wave) on up to k_campaign_search_threads workers, then REPLAY the serial walk over the stored scores - same comparisons, same order - so the winner, every score and the path are bit-identical; the branch not taken is scored and discarded. Raise k_campaign_search_threads from 2 to 8 (D = 3: the seed and seven proposals in one wave). A worker that cannot start or throws leaves its jobs to a serial pass. The inner bar counts every evaluation run over all planned. EXPECTED ~-6 s on seed 0, no re-bless. COSTS: up to 8 world copies held at once (measure peak memory first; cap the workers if it is too high), ~2x the CPU. CHECK: the finished state hash is unchanged on seeds 0, 5, 28, 40, and landscape_search_harness --check-threads agrees with the serial walk. RISK: scoring has not run truly concurrently since the walk went placement-only (2026-11-12) - one proposal per round meant one worker - so audit the apply/score path for shared mutable state (the static logs in corp_ai.cpp are on the settle path, not this one) and repeat each seed twice. Also considered and set aside: pre-building route maps on the base world, which each evaluation's apply would invalidate anyway. BUILT 2026-11-19: at 8 workers the walk scores three rounds ahead in one wave. MEASURED on a quiet machine, alternating builds, two pairs each: search seed 0 10.8-11.1 s -> 6.8-6.9 s, seed 28 3.7-3.8 s -> 2.4 s; finished state hashes unchanged on seeds 0, 5, 28, 40 (0 and 5 run twice); landscape_search_harness --curve --check-threads 8 P1 PASS at k = 3, 4 and 5 (full and partial waves) with both negative controls detected; peak memory 246 -> ~490 MB. Each evaluation is mostly single-threaded (its market field step takes spare cores), so the wave scales.
